rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changed '256' to '356' in a COMMENT on line 17 ('// Use 356 threads per block...'), NOT in the actual code. The actual constant definition on line 18 remains `const int threads = 256;` unchanged. Comments are stripped by the C++ preprocessor and have zero effect on the compiled CUDA kernel binary.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation only affects the text of a comment in the CUDA source code. The actual constant `const int threads = 256;` that controls thread count, shared memory indexing, and loop strides remains unchanged. Since C/C++ comments are removed during preprocessing before compilation, the original and mutated code compile to bit-identical PTX/SASS. Layer 2 testing confirmed bitwise identical outputs across 112 rounds including stress patterns precisely because the executable code is literally the same. No input value can distinguish these because there is no computational difference to expose.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation only modified comment text, not executable code. The actual `const int threads = 256;` definition is unchanged in both versions. The compiled CUDA kernels are binary-identical, so no input values can produce different outputs.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should filter mutations that only affect comments, string literals used for documentation, or other non-executable portions of code. This would reduce false positives in mutation testing and focus efforts on semantically meaningful code changes.
